notes:
Session-context dump for T571 (4×4 single-position leak, claude-opus-5, leaf). Everything below is what the repo does not otherwise record; speculation is labelled. Ordered per the four usual categories.

## (1) Hypotheses formed and ruled out

1. 'The leak is a GLOBAL.F1 writes-ON table artifact' (the bundle's verdict (a), and the study's own caveat). RULED OUT three independent ways: (i) the run's own evidence file records wzo2_path = data/oracle-4x4-v2.wzo2 only, so the checkpoint named alongside it in the caveat was never read; (ii) `grep -c 'ko_ref|memo_writes' src/exp6_solve.zig src/oracle_v2_build.zig` returns 0 and 0, and the WZO2 producer's import closure (oracle_v2_build -> {exp6_solve, artifact2, colex}; exp6_solve -> {artifact, rules, qa023_brute_2x2}) contains neither oracle.zig nor retro.zig, the only two sites of the guard (oracle.zig:253, retro.zig:593); (iii) the guard is not expressible in exp6's fixpoint at all — `d = hist.len - 1` is a search depth along a history path and exp6_solve.zig:1099-1143 is a history-free Jacobi sweep over (board, side, ko, passes) with no hist, no d and no cross-branch memo. Also checked and ruled out: that exp6 seeds from a prior writes-ON artifact — `grep -n 'openFile|readFile|cwd()' src/exp6_solve.zig` hits only the write path at :1741.

2. 'The leak is real — 7 capped games genuinely touch L==H at 4×4' (the bundle's verdict (b)). RULED OUT as stated: it is not a property of the table. Same 500 positions, same table, min-DTT tie-break instead of lowest-cell-index: 0/87 capped games touch L==H. The statement is true only of one tie-break policy.

3. 'The distrusted KO_SENSITIVE column is where the leak lives.' RULED OUT structurally: in WZO2 ko_sensitive is *derived* as L != H (src/artifact2.zig:489), and the counts partition exactly (3,455,412 + 95,677,624 = 99,133,036). An L==H entry is by definition a KO_SENSITIVE-clear entry, i.e. in the column with I4 residual 0/95,677,624. The caveat expressed doubt by pointing at a distrust that cannot reach its own subject. This was the single most useful realisation of the row and it came from reading artifact2.zig, not from any doc.

4. 'untracked/oracle-4x4-writesoff-*.wzo can serve as the writes-OFF comparator.' RULED OUT on provenance before a single value was trusted: the checkpoint file is byte-identical (sha256 28afa11b…) to data/oracle-4x4-parallel.checkpoint.wzo, both untracked files are rules_id=1 (PSK, a ruleset abandoned 2026-07-24), and the bracket file is UNDEF at 25 of the 26 addressable leak states. SPECULATION (not established): the likeliest history is that the T14.1/Track-A run output was copied into data/ under the 'parallel' name (or vice versa) and the two names drifted apart in the docs; the untracked file's mtime (2026-07-27T11:31) is earlier than data/'s (17:01), which is consistent with a copy in that direction but proves nothing about which build produced it.

5. 'data/oracle-4x4-basicko-tie-area.wzo is the same-ruleset comparator that settles it.' RULED OUT: it is rules_id=2 as hoped, and its root matches WZO2 (vb[0] = +1), but it disagrees with WZO2 at 0/26 of the fresh-start leak states and its value column is 94.2 % +-16-or-UNDEF at stride 401 (n=107,349) — inconsistent with a median-pinned V column, since a [-16,+16] bracket pins to 0 and not +-16. T129's own write-up on the same sha256 records 25,000 Bellman violations / 28,000 fresh-start nodes and declares QA-027 FALSE at 4x4. So it is disqualified as a comparator rather than evidence against WZO2 — but what its value column actually holds is UNDETERMINED and is the one loose end this row hands on.

## (2) What the numbers do and do not say

- The 7 was always a sample statistic and the study did not scope it as one: seed 42 gives 7/232, seed 997 gives 3/250, on the same table. Any future citation of '7 capped games' without a seed is quoting noise.
- The bigger correction is one the bundle did not ask for: the 4×4 cap rate is tie-break-dependent too. 145 of 232 capped games at seed 42 (166 of 250 at seed 997) terminate once ties break by DTT. T412's 'capped 46.40 % at 4×4' is a joint measurement of the table and the player. Its 3×3 figure (96.07 %) was not re-measured here and should not be assumed safe by analogy — per-goban independence cuts both ways.
- The random-tie-break control is why the claim is stated negatively. DTT gives 0 and 0; random gives 0 and 1. The defensible statement is 'not invariant under tie-break policy, therefore not a table property', not 'DTT fixes it'.
- Structural, not measured: the DTT tie-break cannot lose value, because it only chooses among children already tied at the best pinned value. Nothing in this row classifies the moves it plays (the probe carries no value_preserving/value_losing classifier; T412's does).

## (3) Instrument and control smells

- The seeded-defect control was wrong on its first build and only 42/45 fired. Cause: the +1 bias was applied to children read from the table but not to double-pass terminal children scored by area_score, so a minimising state whose optimum came from a terminal child could not move. All three misses were passes==1, White to move, with exactly one terminal child. Fixed by biasing terminal children too, and a second reading added (the shift must be exactly +1, now 45/45). This is the whole reason the project's rule is a null control AND a seeded-defect control before the first reading counts: the null control was green from the first run and would have carried a broken instrument.
- The probe copies t412's GameState and chooseWzo2 verbatim rather than re-deriving them. Deliberate (duplication-as-oracle: one in production, the copy as a fixture), but it means a defect in t412's engine is inherited, not detected. What IS independent is the value check: exp6_solve.zig's own generator, a different board encoding (base-3 rank_board4 vs colex), checking values that colex+artifact2 reads back.
- src/t571_leak_probe.zig is additive but NOT wired into build.zig or any battery, so it will rot. Whoever wants it durable should wire it or delete it (SOLUTION-TREE §(b) item 2 is the standing version of this complaint).

## (4) Process observations

- One-writer collision, handled: T573 holds an uncommitted edit to docs/epistemic/SOLUTION-TREE.md §(a) item 5 and §(b) item 1 while this row needed §(b) item 7. Resolved by staging a HEAD-plus-my-hunk blob (`git hash-object -w` then `git update-index --cacheinfo`) so only my hunk is committed and T573's stays in the working tree, uncommitted and intact. Recording the technique because the alternative — committing another row's unfinished work to get your own hunk in — has happened before (see the T493 commit message) and does not have to.
- The bundle's holds= header declared docs/research/loop-onset-2026-08-07.md but the store row had none; `managent claim` warned and used the bundle's holds. A `managent holds --sync` is still owed on the store.
- Cost: three instrument builds (~6 s each) and five guarded runs, each 0.9 s wall and 511 MB peak RSS. The bundle warned the writes-off cross-check could be expensive and preferred a targeted re-solve; the targeted route turned out to be not merely cheaper but the only valid one, because the full-table comparators were disqualified on provenance. Reading the artifact headers (six `xxd -l 96`) before trusting any of them is what caught it, and that cost seconds.
